top_choice_rationale: On public knowledge, Cărtărescu has a distinctive voice and a formal architecture that can be judged across decades. Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid turn memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation into one cumulative imaginative system, and the poetry and essays appear to belong to the same project. The case rests on form and imaginative depth, not on nationality, fame or the number of colleagues who agree. Its main uncertainties remain open: whether the very long late books extend the project or repeat it, how much Romanian verbal texture survives translation, and how thin the translated coverage of the poetry and early prose is. Adonis is a close second. Renewing a poetic language is arguably a larger achievement if it can be verified, but I cannot judge Arabic prosody, so I rank him lower on evidentiary confidence and not on merit. I rank a prize award above no award because both proposals name a single writer with a defensible, form-based citation. I have not read the work directly and claim no independent source verification.
